cells.tense: You are the one tending this now — present in the work of keeping two demands alive at once.
cells.ask: Let one person hear what this cost you, and let their hearing be enough.
cells.core:
When this goes well, tending looks like care that does not exhaust. You hold two demands in the same hand — the thing that needs doing and the thing that needs keeping — and neither one gets dropped, and neither one eats you alive. You feed what is growing without standing over it. What you are becoming is visible in that steadiness, not in what you produce.

Right now you are inside the work and you know it. You are not forcing anything and not letting go of anything. What is left to take in is simple: someone close enough to see what you carried, who says so. That is the acknowledgment you are owed. Let it come toward you today instead of earning it again.
cells.sheetLine: You tend what matters without forcing it, and you are present while you do it.
cells.verb: tending what grows with responsible care

cells.tense: The future has its hands on this — you are bracing against a version of it that has not arrived.
cells.ask: Let one thing be finished enough to enjoy before you start picturing the next one.
cells.core:
When this sits right, tending has a light touch. You give what you can, you let time do some of the work, and you let what is already grown be enough for today. Care that does not clutch. Space that does not squeeze. The difference between tending and gripping is inches wide and miles deep, and going well you are on the tending side.

What is happening instead is that you are living ahead of the growth. Every quiet moment gets used to plan the next move, and every move gets measured against a future nobody can sign yet. The strain is not the work. The strain is carrying loads that have not been handed to you.

The way back is not more effort. Let one thing be done. Sit with what you already made and let it satisfy you — even briefly, even imperfectly. Enjoyment is not slacking. It is what teaches the grip to loosen.

cells.tense: You set the tending down, and you are still standing in the same place, looking at it from where you put it.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you still want, and show up for it once — not because it is working, but because you still want it.
cells.core:
When this sits right, the care comes back on its own. You give, and something grows, and the growth is proof enough to keep going. You trust that what you tend will make the effort worth it. You feed it because the feeding feels good, not because you have already seen the harvest. That is what growing well looks like here — patience with a floor under it, not patience over a hole.

What is happening instead is that the giving stopped. Something behind you did not come back the way you hoped, and the part of you that kept showing up went quiet. You are still here. The thing is not.

What is missing is not the ability to care. It is the willingness to hope in front of an outcome you cannot see. That kind of strength is not stored up somewhere waiting to be found. It shows up when you move first.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped tending it, and you are still standing where you stopped.

cells.tense: The pen is down, but the writing keeps going — you are already shaping what is becoming without naming yourself as the one who shapes it.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, that you are the one who carried something you have been calling the situation's.
cells.core:
When this sits right, you know your own hand in it. You can point at what you kept alive and say, plainly, that you kept it alive. The becoming is not a mystery you witness. It is something you are doing, and you claim it as yours. Tending that anyone can see has less weight to hold alone.

What is happening instead is that it is all happening and none of it is claimed. You talk about how things are going as if the situation were the one doing the tending — as if the care were simply what the moment asked for. The work is real and it is yours, and the saying of it has not happened.

The way back is spoken, not built. Name one thing you gave. Tell one person it was you. What you are becoming does not need defending. It needs to be said.
